testcase.name: conceding in a four-player pod marks the player left and continues the game
conceding in a two-player game still ends the game with the other player winning
the leaver's owned objects leave the game (CR 800.4a)
a creature the leaver stole reverts to its owner (control effect ends, CR 800.4a)
a creature the leaver owns but another player controls leaves the game (CR 800.4a)
the leaver's spells and abilities on the stack cease to exist (CR 800.4a)
combat continues when the leaver's attacker is removed (its blocker stops blocking it)
attackers aimed at the leaver are removed from combat; the rest of the attack stands (CR 800.4e)
a player who has left the game is not a legal attack target (CR 800.4a)
a resolved spell's effect outlives its caster's departure (CR 611.2c) — only source-bound durations end (CR 800.4a)
a departed player's 'until your next turn' effect lasts until that turn would have begun (CR 800.4m)
priority held by the leaver passes to the next player still in the game (CR 800.4a)
the active player conceding hands the turn forward without stalling
conceding while owning the pending decision abandons it instead of deadlocking the table (CR 800.4f–h)
a pending decision addressed to another player survives the leaver's departure
the abandoned decision's priority skips an active player who has also left
